result.process_description:
Title: New Application for Registering for an USI course

If you want to register for a course at the sports institute, you need to select a course.
If slots are free, the system tells you the courses, and dates.
Select one.
Next, you need to check if you already have an account at the sports institute.
If not, you need to check whether you are registered at an eligible university.
If you are, register your account.
If you are not, request an activation and wait for a response.
As soon as you have an account, log into it.
The application is also connected to your twitter account, and lets you tweet to friends who might want to join you, you can complete the registration for the course and provide the payment information.
In the end, you will receive a course ticket.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.
Use a boolean formal conditionExpression on a conditional flow only when the description supports the condition.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Use a complex gateway only for an explicitly described rule that XOR, OR and AND cannot express. Prefer separate split and join gateways for clarity.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.

args.text: When the description states conditional alternatives such as if eligible and if not eligible, model the decision with an exclusive gateway and condition flows. When multiple required activities must both be completed before continuation, model their synchronization with a parallel gateway.

result.rule: When the description makes an action conditional on whether a stated condition holds: Model the condition as a control-flow decision with alternative outgoing paths, so the action is taken only on the applicable path; do not use a gateway with only one incoming and one outgoing sequence flow.

When the description states that one action must occur while another action occurs only if a condition holds: Model the actions as branches from an inclusive gateway, with the mandatory branch always activated and the conditional branch activated when its condition holds; use an inclusive join to synchronize the activated branches before continuing.

When the description says that after a process or activity is complete, several optional follow-up actions may be chosen, including combinations of those actions.: Model the choice with an inclusive gateway and a separate outgoing branch for each optional action, allowing any nonempty combination to be taken.

When the description says that an actor checks whether a condition holds before the process branches: Model the check as a separate activity before the gateway, and use the gateway to represent the resulting alternatives.

args.text: When the description requires multiple distinct activities to be completed before a shared continuation, but specifies no order between them: Model the activities as parallel branches and synchronize them with a parallel join before the continuation.
